chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halbi, from Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, from his father, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked about the immoralities, those of which are apparent and those that are concealed. He said: 'The apparent is the marriage with the wife of one's father, and the concealed is adultery.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between apparent and concealed immorality in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) elucidates the spectrum of *fawahish* (immoralities) by categorizing them into the apparent (*zahir*) and the concealed (*batin*). He identifies marrying one's father's wife as the primary example of public, structural immorality, while adultery represents the quintessential private, sexual transgression. This distinction highlights the comprehensive nature of Islamic ethics, addressing both visible social structures and hidden personal conduct.
